# Surah 89, image section 5: Gözetleme yeri ve bakan göz

## The section's prose (Turkish commentary)

Altıncı ayet dinleyenin gözünü olup bitene çevirir: {ar:أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِعَادٍ, tr:e-lem tera keyfe feale rabbuke bi-Âd, gloss:Rabbinin Âd'a ne yaptığını görmedin mi, source:89:6}. Görmek, gözle ya da kalple bakmaktır: {ar:نظر وإبصار بعين أو بصيرة, tr:nazarun ve ibsârun bi-aynin ev basîra, gloss:gözle ya da basiretle bakıp görmek, source:"ر ء ي,B001"}. Aynı kalıp Fil sahiplerinin akıbetini anlatırken de kullanılır: {ar:أَلَمْ تَرَ كَيْفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصْحَٰبِ ٱلْفِيلِ, tr:e-lem tera keyfe feale rabbuke bi-ashâbi'l-fîl, gloss:Rabbinin fil sahiplerine ne yaptığını görmedin mi, source:105:1}. Dinleyen, bir olayın gözlemcisi yapılır.

Gözlenen şey yolda olan insanlardır. Dördüncü ayetin fiili gece yürüyenleri de adlandırır: {ar:السارية للقوم الذين يسرون بالليل, tr:es-sâriye li'l-kavmi'llezîne yesrûne bi'l-leyl, gloss:sâriye, gece yol alan topluluktur, source:"س ر ي,B001"}. Dokuzuncu ayetteki fiilin yanında ülkeleri boydan boya geçmek duyulur: {ar:جبت البلاد أجوبها وأجيبها واجتبتها إذا قطعتها, tr:cubtu'l-bilâde ecûbuhâ ve ecîbuhâ ve'ctebtuhâ izâ kata'tuhâ, gloss:ülkeleri boydan boya geçtim, source:"ج و ب,B002"}. On birinci ayette bu yolcular ülkelerde sınırı aşar: {ar:مجاوزة الحد في العصيان, tr:mucâvezetu'l-haddi fi'l-isyân, gloss:isyanda sınırı geçmek, source:"ط غ ي,B001"}. Ayetlerin anlamı kazmak ve azmaktır. Yanında yol alan, ülke aşan ve sınırı geçen yolcular duyulur.

On dördüncü ayet yolun üzerindeki yeri adlandırır: {ar:إِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَبِٱلْمِرْصَادِ, tr:inne rabbeke le-bi'l-mirsâd, gloss:Rabbin elbette gözetleme yerindedir, source:89:14}. Mirsâd hem yolun kendisidir, {ar:المرصاد الطريق, tr:el-mirsâd et-tarîk, gloss:mirsâd yoldur, source:"ر ص د,B003"}, hem de gözcünün beklediği yer: {ar:المرصاد المكان الذي يرصد به الراصد, tr:el-mirsâdu'l-mekânu'llezî yersudu bihi'r-râsıd, gloss:mirsâd, gözcünün gözetlediği yerdir, source:"ر ص د,B003"}. Gözcü bir şeyi kollayan kişidir: {ar:الراصد للشئ المراقب له, tr:er-râsıdu li'ş-şey'i el-murâkıbu leh, gloss:râsıd, bir şeyi gözetleyendir, source:"ر ص د,B001"}. Aynı kök yolda pusu kuran yılana da ad verir: {ar:يقال للحية التي ترصد المارة على الطريق رصيد, tr:yukâlu li'l-hayyeti'lletî tersudu'l-mârrate ale't-tarîki rasîd, gloss:yolda geçenleri kollayan yılana rasîd denir, source:"ر ص د,B001"}. Bu düzenin işleyişi şöyledir: gözcü kimseyi kovalamaz, yolun geçtiği yerde bekler. Her yolcu oradan geçmek zorundadır. Bir önceki ayetteki dökme fiili bu yılanın hareketini de anlatır: {ar:صبت الحية عليه إذا ارتفعت فانصبت عليه من فوق, tr:sabbeti'l-hayyetu aleyhi izertefeat fensabbet aleyhi min fevk, gloss:yılan kalkıp yukarıdan üstüne çullandı, source:"ص ب ب,B008"}. Surenin sıralaması da bu düzene uyar. Önce darbe iner, gözetleme yeri ancak sonra adlandırılır. Yolcular gözcünün varlığını vuruldukları anda öğrenir.

Kur'an aynı yeri başka sahnelerde de kurar. Kıyamet anlatılırken cehennem için {ar:إِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ كَانَتْ مِرْصَادًۭا, tr:inne cehenneme kânet mirsâdâ, gloss:cehennem bir gözetleme yeridir, source:78:21} denir. Antlaşmayı bozanlara karşı verilen emir şöyledir: {ar:وَٱقْعُدُوا۟ لَهُمْ كُلَّ مَرْصَدٍۢ, tr:vak'udû lehum kulle marsad, gloss:onlar için her gözetleme yerinde oturun, source:9:5}. İblis de Allah'a şöyle der: {ar:لَأَقْعُدَنَّ لَهُمْ صِرَٰطَكَ ٱلْمُسْتَقِيمَ, tr:le-ek'udenne lehum sırâtake'l-mustekîm, gloss:onlar için senin dosdoğru yolunun üstünde oturacağım, source:7:16}. Şuayb kavmine yollarda pusu kurmamalarını söyler: {ar:وَلَا تَقْعُدُوا۟ بِكُلِّ صِرَٰطٍۢ تُوعِدُونَ, tr:ve lâ tak'udû bi-kulli sırâtin tûidûn, gloss:tehdit ederek her yolun başında oturmayın, source:7:86}. Cinler gökte kendilerini bekleyen bir alev bulur: {ar:يَجِدْ لَهُۥ شِهَابًۭا رَّصَدًۭا, tr:yecid lehû şihâben rasadâ, gloss:kendisini gözetleyen bir alev bulur, source:72:9}. Allah elçisinin önüne ve arkasına gözcüler koyar {source:72:27}. İnsanın söylediği her sözün yanında da hazır bir gözcü vardır: {ar:مَّا يَلْفِظُ مِن قَوْلٍ إِلَّا لَدَيْهِ رَقِيبٌ عَتِيدٌۭ, tr:mâ yelfızu min kavlin illâ ledeyhi rakîbun atîd, gloss:ağzından çıkan her sözün yanında hazır bir gözcü vardır, source:50:18}.

Bakmanın bir de insanın içindeki yüzü vardır. On beşinci ve yirmi üçüncü ayetlerdeki "insan" kelimesi göz bebeğindeki küçük sureti de adlandırır: {ar:إنسان العين المثال الذي يرى في السواد, tr:insânu'l-ayn el-misâlu'llezî yurâ fi's-sevâd, gloss:gözün insanı, gözbebeğinin karasında görünen küçük surettir, source:"ء ن س,B005"}. Bu tanımda misal ve görmek kelimeleri birlikte geçer. Sekizinci ayetin kökü sureti, {ar:التمثال الصورة, tr:et-timsâl es-sûra, gloss:timsal, surettir, source:"م ث ل,B008"}, ve görülerek alınan dersi de adlandırır: {ar:يكون المثل بمعنى العبرة, tr:yekûnu'l-meselu bi-ma'ne'l-ibra, gloss:mesel, ibret anlamına da gelir, source:"م ث ل,B011"}. Beşinci ayetin hicr kökü gözün çevresine de ad verir: {ar:ومحجر العين ما يدور بها, tr:ve mahcaru'l-ayni mâ yedûru bihâ, gloss:gözün mahceri, onu çevreleyen yerdir, source:"ح ج ر,B006"}. Üçüncü ayetteki çift kelimesi de bir tek şeyi iki gören gözü adlandırır: {ar:عين شافعة تنظر نظرين, tr:aynun şâfiatun tenzuru nazarayn, gloss:şâfia göz, iki bakışla bakan gözdür, source:"ش ف ع,B006"}. Sure insana Âd'ı, Semûd'u ve Firavun'u göstermiştir. İnsan ise hemen ardından kendi hâline bakar ve tek bir sınavı iki ayrı hüküm olarak okur: bolluğa ikram, darlığa aşağılanma der. Kur'an bu bakışın kendini nasıl gördüğünü söyler {source:96:7}. Âd'a da kulaklar, gözler ve gönüller verilmişti, ama onlara bir yararı olmadı: {ar:فَمَآ أَغْنَىٰ عَنْهُمْ سَمْعُهُمْ وَلَآ أَبْصَٰرُهُمْ, tr:fe-mâ ağnâ anhum sem'uhum ve lâ ebsâruhum, gloss:ne kulakları ne gözleri onlara bir yarar sağladı, source:46:26}. Kıyamet günü örtü kalkar: {ar:فَكَشَفْنَا عَنكَ غِطَآءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ ٱلْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌۭ, tr:fe-keşefnâ anke ğitâeke fe-basaruke'l-yevme hadîd, gloss:örtünü üstünden kaldırdık, bugün gözün keskindir, source:50:22}.

*** Add File: /Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/_commentary/v16/out/s089/discovery/session-20261005/sec5/terra/followup.tsv
+strong	78:22	root+scene+neighbour	The next ayah identifies the transgressors as the destination for whom Hell waits; it completes 78:21's مِرْصَادًا without making the watchpoint morally indiscriminate.
+strong	52:44	scene+theme	Even if the deniers saw a piece of the sky falling, they would call it a piled cloud; their eye misreads an overhead blow as ordinary weather just as ʿĀd misread the approaching cloud.
+strong	50:36	scene+theme	Destroyed generations stronger in force ranged through the lands but found no escape, an unusually close meeting of country-crossers, the waiting judgment, and the limit no traveler can pass.
+strong	67:15	scene+theme	People are told to walk through the earth's paths and eat God's provision, yet resurrection is to Him; route, measured livelihood, and unavoidable destination share one ayah.
+strong	22:11	scene+theme	The one who worships on an edge is content when good comes but turns away under a trial, enacting the section's division of one divine testing into two opposite verdicts.
+strong	10:21	scene+theme	When people taste mercy after adversity they plot against the signs, while God's messengers record their plotting; changed provision, bad inward reading, and unseen observers coincide.
+strong	16:112	scene+theme	A secure town with abundant provision becomes ungrateful and is made to taste encompassing hunger and fear, directly overturning abundance as proof of lasting honor.
+strong	28:58	scene+theme	Many towns exulting in their livelihood are destroyed and left as scarcely inhabited dwellings, making prosperity's false reading visible in ruins to later observers.
+strong	3:178	scene+theme	Disbelievers must not read divine respite as good for themselves; the delay only lets sin increase before humiliating punishment, matching the watcher who waits rather than chases.
+strong	7:182	scene+theme	Those denying the signs are led gradually toward destruction from where they do not know, a direct statement of the hidden watch disclosed only at the blow.
+strong	7:183	scene+theme+neighbour	God grants the deniers respite because His plan is firm, completing 7:182's unnoticed approach to capture.
+strong	68:44	scene+theme	God tells the messenger to leave the denier to Him, for He will lead such people gradually from where they do not know; the stationary watcher governs the approach.
+strong	68:45	scene+theme+neighbour	The respite granted after 68:44 rests on a firm plan, distinguishing delayed seizure from absence of observation.
+strong	86:15	scene+theme	The opponents devise a plot, setting up the human attempt to control where and when another will be caught.
+strong	86:16	scene+theme+neighbour	God answers their plot with His own plan, disclosing the true watcher behind the apparent ambush of 86:15.
+strong	86:17	scene+theme+neighbour	The command to grant the disbelievers a little respite makes waiting part of the divine counter-plan rather than evidence that they escaped it.
+strong	29:53	scene+theme	Punishment has an appointed time and will come suddenly while its subjects do not perceive, closely matching travelers learning of the watcher only when struck.
+strong	29:54	scene+theme+neighbour	While they demand punishment be hastened, Hell already encompasses the disbelievers; this supplies the unseen surrounding reality behind 29:53's sudden arrival.
+strong	75:10	scene+theme	On that day the human asks where escape lies, posing the road-traveler's question only after the hidden checkpoint has become visible.
+strong	75:11	scene+neighbour	The answer says there is no refuge, closing every alternate route raised by 75:10.
+strong	75:12	scene+theme+neighbour	The final destination that day is to the Lord, completing the no-escape sequence with the place every traveler reaches.
+strong	55:41	scene+theme	Criminals are recognized by their marks and seized by forelocks and feet, so the watcher needs neither pursuit nor testimony to distinguish those arriving.
+strong	34:9	scene+theme	The question asks whether people see what surrounds them of sky and earth before warning of earth swallowing or fragments falling from above; sight, enclosure, and the blow meet directly.
+strong	30:8	scene+theme+neighbour	People are asked whether they reflect within themselves before 30:9 asks them to travel and see former peoples' end, explicitly pairing inward and outward observation.
+strong	25:22	root+scene	When criminals see the angels they receive no good news and cry حِجْرًا مَّحْجُورًا; seeing and the source's h-j-r boundary-word coincide at judgment.
+strong	17:83	theme	Favor makes the human turn away in self-importance, while evil makes him despair, a concise statement of the same two mistaken reactions to one Lord's testing.
+strong	30:36	theme	People rejoice when made to taste mercy and immediately despair when harm from their own deeds reaches them, repeating the divided reading of opposed conditions.
+strong	42:48	theme	A human rejoices at mercy but becomes ungrateful when calamity follows his deeds, another exact contrast in inward responses to changing provision.
+strong	70:19	theme	The human being is created anxiously grasping, introducing the unstable inward disposition behind the section's two judgments.
+strong	70:20	theme+neighbour	When evil touches him he becomes impatient, specifying the deprivation-side response of the human described in 70:19.
+strong	70:21	theme+neighbour	When good touches him he withholds it, completing the paired response and showing that abundance itself exposes rather than certifies him.
+strong	11:9	theme	When mercy is removed after being tasted, the human becomes despairing and ungrateful, explicitly treating deprivation as a final verdict.
+strong	11:10	theme+neighbour	When blessing follows hardship, the human boasts that his troubles are gone, mirroring the opposite error about renewed abundance.
+strong	10:12	scene+theme	Affliction makes a person call on God in every posture, but relief makes him pass on as though he never called, showing self-perception changing with circumstance.
+strong	92:8	theme	The person who is stingy and sees himself self-sufficient repeats the very inward estimate stated in 96:7.
+strong	92:9	theme+neighbour	He denies the finest truth, identifying the moral judgment joined to self-sufficiency in 92:8.
+strong	92:10	scene+theme+neighbour	He is eased toward hardship, a pointed reversal of the ease his wealth seemed to promise.
+strong	92:11	scene+theme+neighbour	His wealth will not avail him when he falls, making the final blow expose the false self-estimate of 92:8.
+strong	104:2	theme	The faulted person gathers and repeatedly counts wealth, fixing his gaze on the very abundance by which he measures himself.
+strong	104:3	scene+theme+neighbour	He thinks his wealth makes him immortal, the most extreme form of reading provision as personal security.
+strong	104:4	scene+theme+neighbour	He will instead be hurled into the Crusher, the sudden destination that overturns the inward verdict in 104:3.
+strong	35:8	scene+theme	A person whose evil deed is beautified so that he sees it as good gives a direct Quranic case of the inward eye manufacturing a false judgment.
+strong	16:26	scene+theme	God attacks plotters' building from its foundations so the roof falls on them from above and punishment comes from where they do not perceive, closely reproducing the hidden watcher and overhead pounce.
+strong	16:45	scene+theme	Those plotting evil are asked whether they feel secure from being swallowed by earth or seized from where they do not perceive.
+strong	16:46	scene+theme+neighbour	God may seize them during their movement about, and they cannot frustrate Him; the travelers' motion does not evade the waiting judgment of 16:45.
+strong	12:107	scene+theme	People are asked whether they feel secure from an encompassing punishment or the Hour arriving suddenly while unaware, directly naming the unperceived encounter.
+strong	3:196	scene+theme	The disbelievers' free movement through the lands must not deceive the observer, warning against reading unhindered travel as escape from the watcher.
+strong	3:197	theme+neighbour	That movement is only brief enjoyment before Hell becomes their resting-place, completing 3:196's correction.
+strong	40:4	scene+theme	The disbelievers' movement through the lands must not deceive the addressee, repeating the warning that apparent freedom on the route is temporary.
+strong	69:9	scene+neighbour	Pharaoh and the overturned towns come with wrongdoing, continuing the observed catalogue from Thamūd and ʿĀd to the third ruler named by the section.
+strong	69:10	scene+theme+neighbour	They disobey their Lord's messenger, so He seizes them with an overwhelming seizure; this supplies the blow joining the peoples listed in 69:5-9.
+strong	51:41	scene+theme	The sending of the barren wind against ʿĀd gives another direct scene of the Lord's action that the observer of 89:6 is asked to see.
+strong	51:42	scene+neighbour	The wind leaves everything it passes like ruins, supplying the visible aftermath of 51:41's divine act.
+strong	51:43	scene+neighbour	Thamūd are granted enjoyment for a time before the thunderbolt of 51:44, making respite precede the blow in the same passage.
+strong	41:16	scene+neighbour	A furious wind is sent against ʿĀd over ill-fated days so they taste disgrace, standing between their self-estimate in 41:15 and Thamūd's blinded choice in 41:17.
+strong	46:27	scene+theme+neighbour	God has destroyed towns around the audience and varied the signs so people might return, turning ʿĀd's sensory failure in 46:24-26 into a road-side warning for later observers.
+contrast	2:250	root+scene+contrast	The believers ask God to pour patience upon them, using ص ب ب for sustaining firmness before battle rather than for a scourge poured upon transgressors.
+contrast	7:126	root+scene+contrast	Pharaoh's threatened believers ask their Lord to pour patience upon them, reversing the source's punitive pour while retaining descent from the true sovereign above Pharaoh.
+contrast	11:11	theme+contrast+neighbour	Those who remain patient and do good are excepted from the despair and boasting in 11:9-10, marking the right response across both conditions.
+contrast	83:15	scene+theme+contrast	The wicked are veiled from their Lord on that day, a boundary on human sight that does not limit the divine watcher who has seen them throughout.
+medium	67:16	scene+theme	The addressees are asked whether they feel secure from the One above causing the earth to swallow them, one half of the above-and-below enclosure completed by 67:17.
+medium	9:55	theme	Wealth and children must not inspire admiration, because they can themselves belong to worldly punishment rather than signal divine favor.
+medium	8:28	theme	Wealth and children are explicitly a trial, directly denying their use as a simple measure of honor.
+medium	64:15	theme	Possessions and children are again named as a test, while the great reward remains with God rather than in the visible abundance.
+medium	20:131	scene+theme	The Prophet is told not to stretch his eyes toward worldly splendor given to groups as a test, and that his Lord's provision is better and more lasting.
+medium	2:155	theme	Fear, hunger, and loss are announced as forms of testing, giving deprivation an explicit purpose other than humiliation.
+medium	18:34	scene+theme	The garden-owner measures himself as greater in wealth and followers, beginning a self-image constructed from visible abundance.
+medium	18:35	scene+theme+neighbour	He enters his garden while wronging himself and declares that it will never perish, turning prosperity into imagined permanent security.
+medium	18:36	scene+theme+neighbour	He doubts the Hour and expects an even better return if brought to his Lord, extending the false wealth-to-honor inference into the Hereafter.
+medium	18:42	scene+theme+neighbour	His produce is encompassed and he wrings his hands over what he spent, the visible collapse that corrects his judgments in 18:34-36.
+medium	68:17	theme	The garden owners are explicitly tested, linking an apparently secure abundance to the trial its possessors fail to recognize.
+medium	68:18	scene+neighbour	They swear to harvest in the morning without making exception, displaying confidence in possession immediately before the unseen visitation.
+medium	68:19	scene+theme+neighbour	A visitation from the Lord circles the garden while they sleep, a night-time watch and blow unknown to its owners.
+medium	68:20	scene+neighbour	The garden becomes dark and stripped by morning, making the hidden visitation of 68:19 visible only in its result.
+medium	100:7	scene+theme	The human is himself a witness to his ingratitude, supporting the section's inward image of the person looking upon his own condition.
+medium	100:8	theme+neighbour	His intense love of wealth names the attachment that distorts the self-witness in 100:7.
+medium	45:23	scene+theme	A person who takes desire as god has hearing and heart sealed and a covering placed over sight, depicting inward appetite disabling the eye's lesson.
+medium	24:43	scene+theme	One driven cloud yields rain and hail that God strikes or averts, while its lightning nearly takes sight; provision, selective overhead blow, and the vulnerable eye occupy one scene.
+medium	17:1	root+scene	The night journey of God's servant from the Sacred Mosque to the farthest mosque is the Quran's signal occurrence of the source's س ر ي night-travel sense.
+medium	51:20	scene+neighbour	Signs in the earth are offered to the certain before 51:21 turns the observing gaze into people's own selves.
+medium	59:18	scene+theme	Every soul is commanded to look at what it has sent forward for tomorrow while God remains aware of its deeds, joining self-inspection to the divine watcher.
+medium	17:14	scene+theme	The person is told to read his own record and is sufficient as a reckoner against himself, a judgment-day form of inward self-observation.
+medium	36:65	scene+theme	Mouths are sealed while hands speak and feet testify to what was earned, revealing that the traveler's own body has preserved the watch.
+medium	24:24	scene+theme	Tongues, hands, and feet testify to what their owners did, turning familiar bodily instruments into ready witnesses.
+medium	58:6	scene+theme	God has enumerated deeds that people forgot and is witness over everything, explaining how the patient watcher can disclose a complete record.
+medium	45:29	scene+theme	The book speaks truth against people because their actions were being transcribed, presenting the stored result of continuous observation.
+medium	18:49	scene+theme	The placed record omits neither small nor great deed, and wrongdoers find what they did present before them, the exhaustive evidence gathered by the watchers.
+medium	15:80	root+scene	The People of al-Ḥijr deny the messengers, naming the historical community behind the rock-cutting Thamūd scene while also sounding the source's h-j-r word.
+medium	15:81	scene+neighbour	God gives the People of al-Ḥijr signs but they turn away, clarifying the failure of perception before their secure dwellings and seizure in 15:82-83.
+medium	56:85	scene+theme	At a person's death God is nearer than the gathered human observers, but they do not see; the unseen divine presence lies inside the visible watching scene.
+medium	6:60	scene+theme	God takes people by night, knows what they earn by day, and raises them until an appointed term before their return and accounting; night, observation, delay, and destination meet.
+medium	76:2	scene+theme	God creates the human from a mixed drop to test him and makes him hearing and seeing, joining trial to the very faculties by which it should be read.
+medium	16:47	scene+theme+neighbour	God may take wrongdoers gradually amid fear, extending 16:45-46's sudden and movement-time seizures with a slower form of the same inescapable watch.
+medium	85:9	scene+theme	The One who owns heaven and earth is witness over everything, grounding the observing stance behind the severe seizure later named in 85:12.
+medium	85:12	scene+theme+neighbour	The Lord's grip is severe, giving the decisive blow that completes the universal witnessing of 85:9.
+medium	6:59	scene+theme	The keys of the unseen belong to God, who knows every falling leaf and hidden grain, expressing a watch from which neither movement nor concealed place escapes.
+medium	34:3	scene+theme	Not even an atom in heaven or earth escapes the Lord, and all is in a clear record; hidden movement and recorded observation are joined.
+medium	99:7	scene+theme	Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, making deeds themselves the final object shown to the observed person.
+medium	99:8	scene+theme	Whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it, completing the exact and morally differentiated disclosure at judgment.
+medium	16:61	scene+theme	God delays people to an appointed term rather than seizing them immediately for wrongdoing, another explicit account of the watcher waiting until the fixed point.
+medium	35:45	scene+theme	God delays creatures to an appointed term instead of taking them at once for what they earn; when the term comes, He has always been seeing His servants.
+medium	53:51	scene+neighbour	God spares none of Thamūd, continuing the destruction of ʿĀd in 53:50 before 53:52 diagnoses Noah's people as still more transgressive.
*** End Patch";
